name: Fold
job: Hold one section closed by default, with a summary line that states its verdict and a grade chip, so the reader can skim every verdict and open only what they need.

anatomy.role: Mono caps group name (Decide, Evidence, System, Method) and a one-line note on what the group holds
A native `details` on the surface, one hairline border; closed by default
h2 in mono caps at the label step, inside the summary
Body text: the fold's answer in one line, so a closed fold still says what it found
28 Chip naming the grade or the count it rests on, in its one colour meaning
A drawn caret that turns a quarter on open; hidden in print
The evidence: any kit organism or molecule, stacked with a 12px gap

states.name: Closed
states.note: The default: title, verdict and chip on one line from a 38rem container.

states.name: Open
states.note: The summary gains a hairline under it and the chevron turns.

states.name: Phone width
states.note: Below 38rem the chip drops under the verdict, left aligned, so the verdict keeps the full line.

use_when: A section has a verdict a reader can act on without opening it.
A page has more than three sections and the reader comes to decide, not to read every word.
avoid_when: Do not hide the next move in a fold: the first screen must carry it.
Do not write a summary that only names the section (Signal); it must state the verdict (He was about to build your tool).

Do not colour the chip for decoration. Colour has one meaning across the kit (arc weld spec 4.3): red a failed check, gold a limit, green proven, cyan an action or focus, plain (steel) unknown, magenta a paradox.

data.note: Optional grouping; the recoil-skim order is Decide, Evidence, System, Method.
`id` is the anchor a skim row links to; `tone` is the chip colour by its one meaning.

access: A native `details` and `summary`: Enter and Space open it, and screen readers announce expanded or collapsed.
A link to a fold's `id` opens it (the page script sets `open` on hash change).
The verdict is text, so the fold reads without colour; the chip names its grade in words.
Print opens every fold (the page script sets `open` before printing); the chevron is hidden in print.
